thingsThatContradictARecordAlreadyInTheR.contradiction: DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 amendment A4 states that West Virginia's § 61-11-26 petition 'costs $200'. The compiled West Virginia profile does not say that.
thingsThatContradictARecordAlreadyInTheR.whereTheClaimIs: data/rcap-grade-a/fable-packet-factory/DETERMINATION_FEE_AND_WAIVER_STANDARD.json, amendment4.a3WasValidatedInTheField: "West Virginia's compiled profile carries three 'no filing fees or costs are charged' lines keyed to section 61-11-25, while the route in hand is a section 61-11-26 petition that costs $200."
thingsThatContradictARecordAlreadyInTheR.whatThisLaneMeasured: src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/WV-west-virginia.json contains ZERO occurrences of '$200'. What it records for 61-11-26, in feeRules and twice more in its fee section, is 'the circuit clerk charges the same fee as filing a civil action, and a person who receives an expungement order must pay a $100 West Virginia State Police processing fee.' The three 'no filing fees or costs are charged' lines keyed to 61-11-25 are exactly as A4 describes them.
thingsThatContradictARecordAlreadyInTheR.whereTheFigureDoesLive: data/rcap-grade-a/route-obligation-census-candidate/route-obligation-candidate.json and packet-family-build-worklist.json both record 'the § 59-1-11(a)(1) civil-action filing fee of $200' for the 61-11-26 families, and one of them adds 'The $100 State Police processing fee is waived by § 61-11-26a(c). The $200 circuit clerk civil filing fee is not waived by the section.'
thingsThatContradictARecordAlreadyInTheR.whyItMatters: A4's substantive holding is untouched — a per-document reading of the profile would still have published 'no filing fee' for a route that costs money, which is the trap A3 was written for. But the amendment attributes the $200 to the compiled profile, and the compiled profile is not where it lives. A lane repairing a West Virginia conviction family by following A4's citation will search the profile, find $100, and not know which record to believe. The same misattribution is printed in a participant-facing packet in this roster, which is why it is a FAIL there and a flag here.
thingsThatContradictARecordAlreadyInTheR.raisedNotDecided: Reported to Captain. This lane changed no determination and no amendment.

thingsThatContradictARecordAlreadyInTheR.contradiction: Two held records describe the Texas $250–$500 range differently, and the tx_exp_acquittal-set packet prints a third description that neither supports.
thingsThatContradictARecordAlreadyInTheR.whatTheRecordsSay: The committed track registry's fees field for trackId tx_exp_acquittal says only 'The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable.' The compiled Texas profile, in filingDestinationRules describing step 4 of this same route, says 'File in a district court for the county of arrest or prosecution (Art. 55A.251). Pay the civil filing fee, which varies by county (often roughly $250–$500 for expunction in many counties; some are lower)' — that is, it attributes the range to the COUNTY CIVIL FILING FEE, which is precisely the fee art. 102.0061(a) makes applicable in district court.
thingsThatContradictARecordAlreadyInTheR.whatThePacketPrints: 'IF YOU HAVE READ THAT EXPUNCTION COSTS $250 TO $500, THAT RANGE IS FROM THE REPEALED STATUTE AND THIS PACKET WILL NOT REPEAT IT', and in the instructions 'The $250-to-$500 range that circulates online comes from the repealed statute.' No held record attributes the range to art. 102.006.
thingsThatContradictARecordAlreadyInTheR.howThisLaneScoredIt: FEE_AND_WAIVER PASS. A1 asks the route-specific record first and the track registry directs the exclusion in terms; a packet that obeys its controlling record is not failing for obeying it, and the fee rule itself is stated, sourced, and complete down to the mandatory waiver subsection and the Rule 145 form. The provenance clause is recorded on the row as a residual conflict, not scored.
thingsThatContradictARecordAlreadyInTheR.theYardstickQuestionForCaptain: May a lane fail FEE_AND_WAIVER on a false PROVENANCE clause when the fee rule it introduces is correct? A4 says a false sentence fails under whichever obligation carries it; A1 says obey the controlling record. Here the controlling record directs the exclusion but not the reason given for it. This lane will not settle that alone, and flags it the way A3 was flagged.

thingsThatContradictARecordAlreadyInTheR.whyNeitherIsScoredAsASourceIdentityFailu: Both pins were traced through git rev-list to real historical blobs — the manifest at commit 148382ab2, the census at 4fb89c96e — and in each case the ROWS the family actually binds were compared between that blob and HEAD and are byte-identical. The manifest moved at 77f24687c for Arizona, California and Utah; the census moved at 7613a4b50 for Montana. Failing a family because another jurisdiction's row moved in a shared national file would put every family that pins one of these into repair on every edit to any state.
thingsThatContradictARecordAlreadyInTheR.theStructuralObservation: A whole-file SHA-256 over a 3.6MB fifty-jurisdiction manifest is not a durable bind for a single state's entry. It will keep drifting, and each drift will cost some verifier the tracing work done here. A per-entry digest, or a pin plus the commit it was taken at, would make the check cheap and exact. Offered as an observation for Captain, not as a change this lane made.

thingsThatContradictARecordAlreadyInTheR.contradiction: The central raster gate records 0 problems over 30 pages for in_section1_petition-set; this lane finds four clipped name appearances on its boundary fixture.
thingsThatContradictARecordAlreadyInTheR.whyBothCanBeTrue: Each flattened widget appearance carries an explicit clip path ('W n', inset 1pt). A clip GUARANTEES that no ink lands outside its box, so a check that looks for ink outside a box cannot see a value truncated inside one. The two instruments answer different questions. This lane's question — does the written value fit the widget that receives it at the size it was set — is the one the Lane C refusal rule is about, and the answer is no in four of sixteen widgets.
thingsThatContradictARecordAlreadyInTheR.whatThisLaneDidNotDo: It did not inspect the raster. It offers this as a gap in coverage to consider, not as a fault in the raster job, which concluded success on its own terms.
